name: subselect_composite_membership
comment: Composite membership: a row value (a, b) in (select a, b …) where the dialect supports row-value IN (SQLite, PostgreSQL); where it does not (SQL Server) the same subquery becomes a correlated EXISTS over derived table s, and the root gains alias t for the correlation — without re-aliasing its columns. Parameters keep one order on every dialect.

sqlite.sql: select user_id, role_id, granted_by, created_at, updated_at from user_roles where ((user_id, role_id) in (select user_id, role_id from user_roles where granted_by is null) and user_id > @c0)

sqlserver.sql: select t.[user_id], t.[role_id], t.[granted_by], t.[created_at], t.[updated_at] from [user_roles] t where (exists (select 1 from (select [user_id], [role_id] from [user_roles] where [granted_by] is null) s where s.[user_id] = t.[user_id] and s.[role_id] = t.[role_id]) and t.[user_id] > @c0)

postgres.sql: select "user_id", "role_id", "granted_by", "created_at", "updated_at" from "user_roles" where (("user_id", "role_id") in (select "user_id", "role_id" from "user_roles" where "granted_by" is null) and "user_id" > @c0)
